challenges.name: bad-release-evidence-quiz
challenges.title: Read the evidence of the release that said OK
challenges.description: Walk through one evidence pack from the checkout incident, step by step: the deploy log, the health-check output, the error-rate graph and the health handler, then the decision to roll back and the check of the fix. Decide for each statement whether the evidence supports it.

questions.question:
Evidence 1 of 4 - the deploy log of checkout v3.2.0 (Tuesday):

14:00:03 deploy checkout v3.2.0 (sha256:7d41e0...) as canary, weight 10%
14:00:41 canary pods ready 2/2 (readinessProbe GET /health -> 200)
14:05:03 gate: GET /health returned 200 on 2/2 canary pods for 300s -> PROMOTE
14:05:04 setWeight 100
14:06:52 rollout complete: 20/20 pods on v3.2.0, ready 20/20

Statement: "According to this log, the canary was promoted because its error rate stayed close to the baseline for five minutes."
questions.explanation: False. The only signal in the log is GET /health: the probe made the pods ready at 14:00:41, and the gate at 14:05:03 promoted because /health returned 200 for 300 seconds. No line mentions an error rate, a baseline or a request count. That is the first finding of the incident: the gate measured whether the process answered, not whether checkout worked. The misconception is that a "green" canary step means someone compared it with the old version.

questions.question:
Evidence 2 of 4 - at 14:09 the on-call engineer calls /health on one v3.2.0 pod, then reads that pod's log:

$ curl -s -w ' %{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' http://10.4.7.21:8080/health
{"status": "ok", "version": "3.2.0"} 200 0.002s

$ kubectl logs checkout-6f9c7b-x2kqp --since=1m | grep ERROR | tail -1
ERROR POST /orders 500 psycopg.OperationalError: connection to server on socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432" failed: No such file or directory

Statement: "Because /health answered 200 in 2 ms on this pod, the pod was able to take orders at 14:09."
questions.explanation: False. In the same minute the same pod failed POST /orders with a database connection error. A 200 from /health only shows that the web server process is running and can answer a request that touches nothing else. The error itself is a clue: libpq tried the default local socket /var/run/postgresql, which is what happens when the connection string is empty. A health check is only as good as what it checks.

questions.question:
Evidence 3 of 4 - the 5xx rate of checkout from the metrics dashboard, as text (1-minute buckets):

time    v3.1.4 (baseline)   v3.2.0 (canary)
13:58   0.3%                -
14:01   0.3%                29.6%
14:03   0.4%                30.9%
14:05   ---- promoted to 100% ----
14:07   -                   31.2%   (all traffic on v3.2.0)
14:09   -                   31.0%

Statement: "The dashboard already showed the canary failing about 100 times more often than the baseline before it was promoted."
questions.explanation: True. At 14:01 and 14:03 the canary's 5xx rate was 29.6% and 30.9% against 0.3% and 0.4% on the baseline, about 100 and 77 times higher, minutes before the 14:05 promotion. The data needed to stop the release existed; the gate did not look at it. Comparing rates with a baseline over the same minutes is exactly what the canary gate of the previous lesson does.

True. DATABASE_URL is not set in the pod (the Deployment still sets DB_URL), so os.environ.get returns "" and every connection attempt fails - that is the OperationalError of evidence 2. With open=False the pool only tries on the first query, so start-up succeeded and health() never noticed. A check that actually uses the database fails at once, the readiness probe keeps the canary at 0 ready pods, and the gate never sees a healthy step. Checking the config at start-up (refusing to start without DATABASE_URL) would have caught it even earlier.

questions.question:
At 14:12, 31% of checkout requests fail. You have saved the four pieces of evidence above. A teammate says the code diff of v3.2.0 is 1,400 lines and asks to keep v3.2.0 running "until we know exactly which line broke it". The previous release is recorded in the deploy log as checkout v3.1.4 (sha256:2b9a55...).

Statement: "Keeping v3.2.0 running until the broken line is found is the better choice, because rolling back would destroy the evidence needed to fix it."
questions.explanation: False. Users are failing now, the previous version is known by digest, and rolling back is a one-minute traffic change. The evidence is already saved (logs, metrics, the deploy log), and the broken image still exists in the registry, so it can be run again in staging to debug. The order is: stop the damage (roll back), then find the cause, then fix and verify. Debugging in production while 31% of orders fail turns a 10-minute incident into an hour-long one.

questions.question:
After the rollback, the 5xx rate is back at 0.3% on v3.1.4 at 14:16. The fix, v3.2.1, adds GET /ready, which returns 503 unless every required variable is set and SELECT 1 on the database answers within 500 ms; the readinessProbe now calls /ready. To test the readiness check on its own, the team deploys v3.2.1 to staging with its start-up config check switched off and the old Deployment that still sets only DB_URL:

14:40:02 deploy checkout v3.2.1 as canary, weight 10%
14:40:38 pod checkout-staging-5d1-q8r2t: GET /ready -> 503 {"ready": false, "problems": ["config DATABASE_URL is not set", "database: OperationalError"]}
14:45:02 gate: canary pods ready 0/2 -> HOLD, no traffic sent to v3.2.1

Statement: "This staging run shows that the new readiness check would stop the same mistake before any user sent traffic to it."
questions.explanation: True. The same missing variable now makes /ready return 503 with the reason, the canary has 0 of 2 ready pods, and the gate holds without sending traffic. That is how you verify a fix to a health check: reproduce the original failure on purpose and watch the check catch it. A check that has never been seen failing is not yet a check you can trust.

challenges.name: fix-readiness-check
challenges.title: Fix the readiness check that still says ready too easily
challenges.description: After the incident, Rice Rocket's checkout got a real readiness endpoint: GET /ready returns readiness(snapshot), and Kubernetes sends traffic to a pod only while it answers 200. On staging it still let broken pods through. A pod whose DATABASE_URL was set to an empty string reported ready. A pod whose database answered SELECT 1 in 2.4 seconds, with a 500 ms timeout, reported ready. And when a broken metrics exporter sent the check result ok as the string "false", the pod reported ready as well. Fix the functions in readiness.py so they follow the rules in the docstring: every problem is listed (config first, then checks in order), with the exact texts given there, and the answer is {"status": 200, "ready": true, "problems": []} or status 503 with ready false. The runner at the bottom (do not change it) reads one snapshot from stdin and prints the answer as JSON.
hints: Run the three staging cases from the description through the code in your head: an empty DATABASE_URL, a database check with ok true and latency_ms 2400, and a check whose ok is the string "false". At which line does each one slip through as healthy?

Look at how config_problems decides that a variable is set, and at the first if in check_problems: which values of ok does a plain truth test accept? Also notice which parameter of check_problems is never used.

A similar check on different input: a disk check gets {"used_pct": "95"} and a limit of 90. `"   ".strip() == ""` is True, `bool("false")` is True, `isinstance(1, bool)` is False and `isinstance(False, bool)` is True. So the check first asks "is used_pct a number at all?" (otherwise "disk: invalid result"), and only then compares it with the limit, where exactly 90 still passes.

tests.name: All config set and both checks answer in time: 200, ready
The incident: DATABASE_URL is set but empty, so the pod must not be ready
The database says ok but takes 2400 ms with a 500 ms timeout: not ready
A spaces-only value is not set; a failed check without error text says failed
Broken exporter: ok as the string "false", as 1, as null or missing is an invalid result
Edge: nothing required and a check at exactly the timeout is still ready
Several problems at once: config first in order, then checks in list order
Large: 400 variables and 300 checks, six problems hidden among them
